account: Gastroenterologists at Korea University College of Medicine and Ewha Womans University College of Medicine ran a randomized trial at two tertiary hospitals in Seoul, South Korea, from May 2023 to April 2025. They randomly assigned 998 adults who had screening, surveillance or diagnostic colonoscopy to colonoscopy with or without ENAD-DET-01, a deep-learning detection system from Ainex Corporation of Seoul. The system draws a circle on the endoscopy monitor when it recognizes a polyp. Adenomas were found in 52.3% of patients in the system group and in 36.1% of the control group. Polyps were found in 72.2% against 54.5%, and the system group had 1.2 adenomas per colonoscopy against 0.8. The system did not raise the detection of sessile serrated lesions or cancers. Both hospitals used the same Olympus endoscopy platform. The Korea Medical Device Development Fund paid for the study, and the authors report no conflicts of interest.
